from.place: The coherent homotopy-equivalence cell and its pushout/lifting calculations, needed for fibrations in the quasi-equivalence model in proof paragraph 2.

title: Coherent homotopy-equivalence cell: realization, pushout and lifting
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and use the cochain dg categories and free adjoining constructions of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus]. Let $K_R$ be the free $R$-linear dg category on objects $0,1$ and arrows $f:0\to1$, $g:1\to0$ of degree $0$, $r_0:0\to0$ and $r_1:1\to1$ of degree $-1$, and $t:0\to1$ of degree $-2$, with
$$df=dg=0,\qquad dr_0=gf-1_0,\qquad dr_1=fg-1_1,\qquad dt=fr_0-r_1f.$$
Composition is written right to left. Let $i:\mathbf1_R\to K_R$ select object $0$. Write $H^0(\mathcal C)$ for the category with the same objects as $\mathcal C$ and morphisms $H^0(\mathcal C(x,y))$; a quasi-isomorphism of complexes induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group.

(a) Every closed degree-zero arrow $u:x\to y$ in a dg category $\mathcal B$ whose class in $H^0(\mathcal B)$ is invertible extends to a dg functor $K_R\to\mathcal B$ taking $f$ to $u$.

(b) For any dg category $\mathcal C$ and $c\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal E=\mathcal C\amalg_{\mathbf1_R}K_R$, with $\mathbf1_R\to\mathcal C$ selecting $c$. For all old objects $x,y$ the map $\mathcal C(x,y)\to\mathcal E(x,y)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The object set of $\mathcal E$ has just one additional object, the image of $1\in K_R$, and that object is isomorphic to $c$ in $H^0(\mathcal E)$.

(c) Suppose $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is degreewise surjective on every morphism complex, a commutative square with left side $i$ and right side $p$ is given, and a closed degree-zero $u:x\to x'$ in $\mathcal C$ is specified with $[u]$ invertible in $H^0(\mathcal C)$, source $x$ the object of the top functor $\mathbf1_R\to\mathcal C$, $p(x')$ equal to the image of $1$ in the bottom functor $K_R\to\mathcal D$, and $p(u)$ equal to its image of $f$. Then the square has a dg-functor filler $K_R\to\mathcal C$ taking $f$ to $u$. In particular all the prescribed images of $g,r_0,r_1,t$ lift simultaneously, with their displayed differential identities.

source.place: Chapter 1, section 1.3.1, definition of K on printed p. 27, Proposition 1.7, Lemma 1.10 and proof of Proposition 1.13, printed pp. 27-32. Cochain degree convention as displayed. Read online; not locally archived. No corresponding Stacks tag.

proof.text: First the specified differential defines a dg category: its square is zero on $f,g,r_0,r_1$, and $d(fr_0-r_1f)=f(gf-1)-(fg-1)f=0$. Extend it to words by the signed Leibniz rule, using the free dg presentation. For (a), choose a closed $v:y\to x$ representing $[u]^{-1}$ and degree-$-1$ arrows $a,b$ with $da=vu-1_x$ and $db=uv-1_y$. Such choices mean exactly that the two compositions represent the identity in $H^0$. Put $z=ua-bu$; then $dz=u(vu-1)-(uv-1)u=0$. Set $b'=b+zv$ and $w=za$. Directly $db'=uv-1_y$ and $dw=-z( vu-1_x)=ua-b'u$. The assignment $f\mapsto u$, $g\mapsto v$, $r_0\mapsto a$, $r_1\mapsto b'$, $t\mapsto w$ respects every differential and hence extends by the free presentation. This proves (a) without a cone-contractibility criterion.

source.place: Proposition 1.7 and Proposition 1.13, realization; explicit correction of the chosen inverse homotopies supplied here.

proof.text: Record the cone matrix dictionary, to be used twice below. In the cone enlargement of the cited node, for a closed $u:x\to y$ write a degree-$-1$ endomorphism of $C_u=h_y\oplus h_x[1]$ as $H=\begin{pmatrix}-b&-w\\ v&a\end{pmatrix}$. Computing $\partial H=D_uH+HD_u$ gives the four entries $-db+uv$, $-dw+ua-bu$, $-dv$, and $vu-da$, respectively. Thus $\partial H=1$ is exactly the four equations $dv=0$, $da=vu-1_x$, $db=uv-1_y$, $dw=ua-bu$. The correspondence is entrywise, bijective and commutes with dg functors. The minus signs in the upper row implement our cochain-shift convention.

source.place: Proposition 1.7, printed p. 27; matrix multiplication with cochain-shift signs made explicit.

proof.text: For (b), let $\mathcal L_0$ be obtained from $\mathcal C$ by adding a new object $H$ with endomorphisms $R$, initially no morphisms to or from old objects, and then a free closed arrow $s:c\to H$ of degree zero. Equivalently adjoin the object first and then the complex $R[0]$ of arrows. The free-word formula shows that $\mathcal L_0(X,Y)=\mathcal C(X,Y)$ for old $X,Y$, that $\mathcal L_0(X,H)=s\mathcal C(X,c)$ for old $X$, and that $\mathcal L_0(H,Y)=0$ for old $Y$. In particular postcomposition by $s$ is an isomorphism of complexes $\mathcal L_0(X,c)\to\mathcal L_0(X,H)$. Let $\mathcal L_1$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal L_0)$ on all labelled representables and $Z=C_s$. Its old-object morphism complexes remain exactly those of $\mathcal L_0$.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: L_0, Yoneda and L_1; the free-arrow Hom calculation written out.

proof.text: Freely adjoin $h:Z\to Z$ of degree $-1$ with $dh=1_Z$ to $\mathcal L_1$, giving $\mathcal L_2$, and restrict to the labels of $\mathcal L_0$ to obtain $\mathcal L_3$. Apply [lem-coef-dgcat-cell-comparison-functors] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal L_0$ and $u=s$. Its category $\mathcal B$ is the pushout $\mathcal E$: both freely adjoin precisely $g,r_0,r_1,t$ to $\mathcal L_0$ with the equations in the statement. The free presentations identify them over $\mathcal L_0$. We obtain dg functors $F:\mathcal E\to\mathcal L_3$ and $G:\mathcal L_3\to\mathcal E$, both fixing $\mathcal L_0$, with $F(g)=v_h$, $F(r_0)=a_h$, $F(r_1)=b_h$, $F(t)=w_h$ and $G$ taking these four entries back to the respective generators.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: M=L_3 comparison and inverse verification; extracted into two cited lemmas for the 2026-10-17 repair.

proof.text: The composite $GF$ fixes every coefficient of $\mathcal L_0$ and each of $g,r_0,r_1,t$ by the displayed values of the comparison functors. Every arrow of the free presentation of $\mathcal E$ is a finite linear combination of words in these coefficients and generators. Applying $GF$ termwise therefore fixes it, so $GF=1_{\mathcal E}$.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: M=L_3 comparison and inverse verification; extracted into two cited lemmas for the 2026-10-17 repair.

proof.text: The composite $FG$ fixes every coefficient of $\mathcal L_0$ and each of $v_h,a_h,b_h,w_h$. Apply [lem-coef-dgcat-cone-word-normal-form] with $\mathcal A=\mathcal L_0$ and $u=s$: its generation and functor-equality conclusion gives $FG=1_{\mathcal L_3}$. Thus $\mathcal E$ is strictly isomorphic to $\mathcal L_3$ over $\mathcal L_0$, identifying their morphism complexes, not merely their homotopy categories.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 29: M=L_3 comparison and inverse verification; extracted into two cited lemmas for the 2026-10-17 repair.

proof.text:
For old $X,Y$, apply the free-arrow filtration to $\mathcal L_1\to\mathcal L_2$ at the arrow $h$. Its length-zero term is $\mathcal C(X,Y)$. For $m\geq1$ the length-$m$ quotient is the tensor complex
$$\mathcal L_1(Z,Y)\otimes_R Rh\otimes_R(\mathcal L_1(Z,Z)\otimes_R Rh)^{\otimes_R(m-1)}\otimes_R\mathcal L_1(X,Z),$$
where $Rh$ is $R$ in degree $-1$ with zero differential. The terms differentiating $h$ lower length because $dh=1_Z$. The filtration is exhaustive and its inclusions split as graded modules. These statements are precisely the arbitrary-arrow-degree case of the cited free-cell lemma; no tensor product is being assumed to preserve a mere quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed pp. 29-30: length filtration for the freely adjoined contraction.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal C(X,c)$. The cone Hom formula and step 3 identify $\mathcal L_1(X,Z)$ with the cone of $1_A$, whose differential on $A^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ is $(a,b)\mapsto(da+b,-db)$. The degree-$-1$ map $k(a,b)=(0,a)$ satisfies $dk+kd=1$. Consequently each positive-length quotient in step 7 is contractible, even when the other Hom complexes are nonflat: if $T$ denotes all preceding tensor factors, the degree-$-1$ operator on $T\otimes\mathcal L_1(X,Z)$ is $q\otimes v\mapsto(-1)^{|q|}q\otimes k(v)$. The tensor differential gives $dK+Kd=1$ by cancelling the two terms involving $dq$.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 30: cone of the isomorphism s_*; explicit contraction and tensor sign.

proof.text: Here is the filtration argument without a convergence assumption. In $F_m/F_0$ every cycle has a top-length component. Since $F_m/F_{m-1}$ is contractible for $m>0$, that component is a boundary; subtract the differential of a graded lift of a primitive to reduce its length. Induction on $m$ makes it zero modulo $F_0$, proving $F_m/F_0$ acyclic. Every element of $\bigcup_m F_m/F_0$ has finite length, so the same finite induction proves the union quotient acyclic. Finally the inclusion $F_0\to\bigcup_mF_m$ is a cohomology isomorphism directly: a cycle projects to a boundary in the quotient, so subtract a lifted boundary to obtain a cycle in $F_0$; if a cycle in $F_0$ bounds upstairs, its primitive projects to a cycle in the quotient, and subtracting a lifted primitive there puts that bounding element in $F_0$. All lifts used here exist degreewise. Together with steps 4–6 this proves the old-object quasi-isomorphisms of (b).

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 30: exhaustive filtration argument expanded by finite-length cycle and boundary reduction.

proof.text: The object set in the presentation of $\mathcal E$ consists of the old objects and exactly the new label $H$; adjoining arrows changes no objects. Its closed arrows $f:c\to H$ and $g:H\to c$ satisfy $gf-1_c=dr_0$ and $fg-1_H=dr_1$. Their $H^0$ classes are inverse, so $H$ is isomorphic to $c$ in $H^0(\mathcal E)$. This finishes (b). The temporary cone object $Z$ is omitted when taking $\mathcal L_3$; it is not an extra object of the pushout.

source.place: Lemma 1.10, printed p. 30: essential surjectivity, with the new-object bookkeeping clarified.

proof.text: For (c), keep the specified closed arrow $u:x\to x'$ fixed throughout. In the functorial cone enlargements form $C_u$ and $C_{p(u)}$ and their endomorphism dg algebras $A$ and $B$. The functor $p$ induces a unital dg algebra map $P:A\to B$. Each homogeneous endomorphism is a four-entry matrix in shifts of the original Hom modules; degreewise surjectivity of $p$ on those four Hom complexes therefore makes $P$ degreewise surjective. By (a) and the matrix dictionary of step 2 there is $h_0\in A^{-1}$ with $dh_0=1$. The given bottom functor supplies, by that same dictionary, a particular $h_D\in B^{-1}$ with $dh_D=1$. This uses no equivalence or acyclicity hypothesis on $p$ and changes none of its prescribed bottom entries.

source.place: Proposition 1.13, printed p. 32: cone endomorphism map, its degreewise surjectivity and the supplied contractions.

proof.text: Choose any graded lift $k\in A^{-1}$ of $h_D$, and let $e=dk-1\in A^0$. Then $de=0$ and $P(e)=0$. Set $h=k-h_0e$. The signed Leibniz rule gives $d(h_0e)=e$, so $dh=1$, and $P(h)=h_D$ because $P(e)=0$. By the four-entry dictionary, $h$ now gives lifts of precisely the prescribed $g,r_0,r_1,t$ satisfying all four equations simultaneously. The fixed $u$ remains the image of $f$. The free presentation extends these images to the required dg-functor filler; the object equalities in the hypothesis make both sides of the square strict. This proves (c).

source.place: Proposition 1.13, printed p. 32: contraction lifting, here proved by the explicit kernel correction k-h_0(dk-1).
